alternative_explanations: Thirty examples may raise execution costs disproportionately; grammar ordering rather than learned reuse may explain compression; discovery and state may scale poorly with K; the oracle may continue to dominate.
confounds: The full truth table minus one is synthetic and unusually informative; program length and the hand-designed DSL are known; the benchmark is visible to the implementation.
falsification_criteria: Kill this program-library line if any non-random solver is inexact, learned search is worse than primitive search, macro selection is below 8 of 9 conditions, learned search has no average gain, or the mismatched library reproduces the gain.

outcome_policy.negative: Ambiguity was not the sole defect or the family is too weak to support the claim; reduce confidence, close the family, and pivot.
outcome_policy.null: Removing ambiguity restores correctness but does not yield a robust amortized advantage or Pareto improvement; close the family and pivot.
outcome_policy.positive: Behavioral ambiguity caused the v2 accuracy defect and learned fragment reuse robustly compresses exact search in this family; record the correction, then pivot to a radically different task family.

predicted_outcome: All non-random solvers reach accuracy 1.0 for every seed, K, and depth; learned_library_search selects the true macro in all 9 seed-by-K conditions, has seed CV at most 0.10, and at K=128 reduces amortized cold operations by at least 30% versus primitive search at depths 4 and 6 without regressing at depth 8.
promotion_criteria: Promotion requires exactness, robust selection, a material amortized gain, bounded variance, and a Pareto improvement after query, update, state, and discovery costs; matching the oracle alone is insufficient.
research_question: Does removing behavioral ambiguity restore exactness while preserving learned search compression?
title: Program library identifiable v3 corrective screen
